questions.prompt: Which of the following improper integrals converges to a finite value?

feedback.hint: Use the p-test: ∫ from 1 to ∞ of x⁻ᵖ dx converges if and only if p > 1.
feedback.solution: With p = 2 the antiderivative −1/x gives the value 1, so the integral converges. For p = 1 and p = 1/2 the antiderivative grows without bound, and a constant integrand grows linearly, so those diverge.

questions.prompt: The degree-2 Taylor polynomial of eˣ at 0 is used to estimate e^0.5. Use the Lagrange remainder bound |R₂| ≤ M|x|³/3! with M = e^0.5 ≈ 1.6487 to bound the error. Enter a number.

feedback.hint: On [0, 0.5] the third derivative of eˣ is at most e^0.5.
feedback.solution: |R₂| ≤ 1.6487 × 0.5³ ÷ 6 = 0.0343. The polynomial gives 1.625, and the true value 1.6487 differs by 0.0237, which is inside the bound.

questions.prompt: A spring-like force F(x) = 4x newtons acts along a displacement from x = 0 to x = 3 m. Calculate the work done. Enter a value and unit.

feedback.hint: Integrate the force over the displacement.
feedback.solution: W = ∫₀³ 4x dx = 2x² evaluated from 0 to 3 = 18 N·m = 18 J. The units come from newtons times meters.

questions.prompt: The alternating series Σ (−1)ⁿ⁺¹/n² is truncated after 4 terms. Use the alternating-series error bound to state the largest possible absolute error. Enter a number.

feedback.hint: The error is at most the first omitted term.
feedback.solution: The first omitted term is 1/5² = 0.04. For an alternating series whose terms decrease to zero, the truncation error is no larger than the first omitted term in magnitude.
